sections.h2: A spirulina batch is ready in 15-18 days, against 90-120 for a cereal crop

chart.title: One spirulina pond can turn over several batches in a cereal crop's cycle
chart.sub: Days from start to harvestable density, per cycle.
chart.source: Cultivation and crop-cycle figures as stated in the post, Section 1.

sections.means: Batches take roughly 15-18 days, so one pond can harvest several times in a season, while cereal cycles take 90-120 days.
sections.todo: Check the batch-cycle figures against a grower's own harvest log before using them in any farm-income plan.

sections.h2: One study reports a 46-67% cut in malnutrition, yet a trial saw beta-carotene fall 40%

chart.title: Reported malnutrition gains and a counter-finding point in opposite directions
chart.sub: Percent change as reported; the negative bar is a fall in beta-carotene, not a gain.
chart.source: Haryana and Karnataka programme reporting; National Institute of Nutrition trial coverage, as cited in the post.
rows: Child malnutrition, reduction reported in one study
Beta-carotene in children, drop in NIN trial

sections.means: Pilot programmes report large malnutrition cuts, but a national institute trial found beta-carotene falling, so the case remains unsettled.
sections.todo: Wait for independently verified trial results before treating spirulina as a supplement for malnourished children.

sections.h2: China produces 45-65% of world spirulina, depending on the estimate

chart.title: Estimates of China's share differ by source, so quote it as a range
chart.sub: China's share of world spirulina production, %, by source.
chart.source: China Ministry of Agriculture (2025) and other industry trackers, as cited in the post.

sections.means: China's own agriculture ministry puts its share at 45%, while other industry trackers put it at 55-65%, and the post reports both.
sections.todo: Quote China's share as a range with both sources named, since the estimates differ by source.
